scope: Windows production Rust MediaPlan export functions, built headless with the optional vulkan-export feature. Real video is decoded on the CPU and uploaded; Skia composition and FFmpeg Vulkan Video encoding do not read rendered images back to the CPU. Multi-frame asynchronous rendering is not included.

cases: danmu real-video background, subtitle alpha, copied audio, and preserving the previous output
complete capability probe: blue background and non-linear half-transparent red overlay in all three compressed frames
moving-video full decoded frame/PTS grid, copied audio, matching temporal samples, and changing content
project cancellation preserves the previous output and releases resources
project segments preserve audio/cache behavior and the previous output

vulkan_validation.known_sdk_issue: The unmodified FFmpeg 9.0.2 baseline retains queued Vulkan encoder image views at device destruction. Upstream FFmpeg commit ddfa842088cd86bd48bc4533f10a4b5badcbd02d fixes this; the backport source patch is archived in scripts/ffmpeg-sdk-patches. A matching replacement SDK has not yet passed this run.

vulkan_api_capture.transport: Complete process stdout, including all Vulkan instance/device lifetimes; independent verify.py ignores non-API test lines.

trace.scope: Recorded application Vulkan calls; buffer mapping and opaque driver internals are not classified as image readback

vulkan_api_capture.readback_scope: Zero recorded image-to-host Vulkan copy commands. Buffer mappings include encoded bitstream access; CPU-decoded base-frame and texture uploads remain. This does not establish opaque driver internals or GPU video decoding.

limitations: Optional feature; GUI packaging and default release SDK selection are outside this headless validation.
The known FFmpeg 9.0.2 cleanup error prevents claiming a clean validation-layer run.
The elapsed times are correctness-test durations, not an export performance benchmark.
